interest: Covers postwar US intelligence tracking Japanese national Kikue Kato, a wartime Paris liaison worker, through a multinational repatriation process.
overview: This file (decimal file 894.20251) documents the intelligence screening, surveillance, and eventual repatriation of Kikue Kato (Kikué Kato), a Japanese national residing in Paris from 1937 to 1947 who was suspected of wartime intelligence and propaganda activities. Having served as a secretary for the South Manchuria Railway's Paris office and the Japanese Military Attaché, as well as an alleged wartime liaison with Japanese groups in Switzerland, Kato sought to return to Japan in late 1946. Her visa applications prompted investigation by the Strategic Services Unit (SSU) and the Central Intelligence Group (CIG) due to potential espionage concerns and suspected ties between her Russian companion, Pierre Tchelebi, and French and Soviet communist groups—suspicions that subsequent inquiries largely discounted. The documents record the inter-agency and diplomatic correspondence among the State Department, SSU/CIG, the Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SCAP) and U.S. Political Adviser in Tokyo, the Japanese Government, and the French Mission in Japan, tracing Kato's journey from Paris through Marseilles and Saigon to her arrival in Japan aboard the S.S. General Gordon in August 1947.

people.name: Kikue Kato
people.role: Japanese national in France; former employee of the South Manchuria Railway and Japanese Military Attaché's office in Paris; nurse to Mr. Butan's children; prospective employee of the French Embassy in Tokyo

people.name: Lester C. Houck
people.role: Chief, Dissemination Branch, SO, Strategic Services Unit; later Chief, Source Control Branch, SO, Central Intelligence Group

people.name: Pierre Tchelebi
people.role: Russian émigré residing in Paris; husband or companion of Kikue Kato

people.name: Monsieur Pierre
people.role: Russian émigré associated with political negotiations for the Union des Patriotes Soviétiques and contact of the Communist Ligne Intérieure and French Communist Party

people.name: George Atcheson Jr.
people.role: United States Political Adviser to the Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SCAP), Tokyo

subfiles.about: GSA withdrawal notice for a classified document removed from file 894.20251/3-2245.

subfiles.about: SSU intelligence report detailing Kikue Kato's wartime activities in Paris and suspected communist connections, transmitted to the State Department.
subfiles.from: Lester C. Houck, Chief, Dissemination Branch, SO, Strategic Services Unit
subfiles.summary: SSU report DB-1982: Kikue Kato, a Japanese Paris resident seeking repatriation, had wartime ties to the South Manchuria Railway and Japan's Military Attaché, plus a suspected Soviet-linked Russian companion, 'Monsieur Pierre'.
subfiles.title: SSU Intelligence Report DB-1982 on Kikue Kato with Transmittal Memorandum
subfiles.to: Jack D. Neal, Department of State

subfiles.about: State Department airgram transmitting SSU intelligence on Kikue Kato to the U.S. Political Adviser in Tokyo.
subfiles.from: Department of State (Dean Acheson, Acting Secretary of State)
subfiles.summary: Airgram A-173: Acheson alerts SCAP Tokyo that Kikue Kato, a wartime Japanese intelligence/propaganda worker in Paris, is seeking to return to Japan, flagging her visa status and ties to suspected communist 'Monsieur Pierre'.
subfiles.title: State Department Airgram A-173 to USPOLAD Tokyo Concerning Kikue Kato
subfiles.to: United States Political Adviser to SCAP, Tokyo

subfiles.about: USPOLAD Tokyo airgram forwarding a SCAP G-2 biographical profile of Kikue Kato to the State Department.
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser, Tokyo (George Atcheson Jr.)
subfiles.summary: Airgram A-15: SCAP G-2 biographical sketch of Kikue Kato details her education, Foreign Ministry and French-firm employment, and her 1937 trip to France as a nanny aboard the André Lebon.
subfiles.title: USPOLAD Tokyo Airgram A-15 Transmitting SCAP G-2 Biographical Sketch of Kikue Kato

subfiles.about: CIG report clearing Kikue Kato's companion of communist ties and reporting French assistance for her repatriation.
subfiles.from: Lester C. Houck, Chief, Source Control Branch, SO, Central Intelligence Group
subfiles.summary: CIG report DB-3295: the French Foreign Office helped resolve Kikue Kato's travel issues; her companion is identified as Pierre Tchelebi, not the suspected communist 'Monsieur Pierre'.
subfiles.title: CIG Intelligence Report DB-3295 on Kikue Kato with Transmittal Memorandum
subfiles.to: Jack D. Neal, Department of State

subfiles.about: USPOLAD Tokyo despatch reporting Japanese Government and French Mission communications regarding Kato's transit through Saigon.
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo (H. Earle Russell for George Atcheson Jr.)
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 1147: USPOLAD Tokyo reports Kikue Kato reached Saigon en route home and awaits the next ship to Japan.
subfiles.title: USPOLAD Tokyo Despatch No. 1147 on the Repatriation of Kikue Kato

subfiles.about: Memorandum from the French Mission in Japan confirming Kato's arrival in Saigon and scheduled embarkation for Japan.
subfiles.from: French Mission in Japan (Mission Française au Japon)
subfiles.summary: French Mission memo confirms Kikue Kato's arrival in Saigon and that she will board the next Japan-bound vessel.
subfiles.title: French Mission in Japan Memorandum No. 187 on Kikue Kato's Repatriation
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers, Diplomatic Section

subfiles.about: USPOLAD Tokyo despatch confirming Kikue Kato's repatriation to Japan aboard the S.S. General Gordon.
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo (Counselor of Mission / H. Earle Russell)
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 1278 confirms Kikue Kato was repatriated to Japan on August 27, 1947, aboard the S.S. General Gordon.
subfiles.title: USPOLAD Tokyo Despatch No. 1278 on Kikue Kato's Return to Japan
